content: Orlistat is a medication prescribed to aid in weight loss and prevent weight regain. It is typically used in conjunction with a doctor-approved exercise program, behavioral changes, and a reduced-calorie diet. This medication is particularly beneficial for individuals who are overweight or obese, especially those with weight-related medical conditions. Orlistat works by inhibiting the enzyme responsible for breaking down dietary fats, preventing their absorption, and allowing the undigested fat to be excreted through bowel movements. When taking orlistat, follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. It is usually taken orally three times daily, with liquid, during or within one hour after a meal containing fat. If you skip a meal or consume a meal without fat, you should also skip that dose of orlistat. Do not increase your dose or use this medication more frequently or for longer than prescribed. Orlistat can interfere with the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K). Therefore, it is recommended to take a daily multivitamin supplement containing these nutrients, ideally at least two hours before or after taking orlistat. Weight loss may become noticeable within two weeks of starting orlistat. Common side effects of orlistat include changes in bowel habits due to unabsorbed fat. These may include fatty or oily stools, oily spotting, intestinal gas with discharge, an urgent need to have a bowel movement, increased frequency of bowel movements, or poor bowel control. These effects may worsen if you consume more fat than recommended. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to orlistat are rare. Before starting orlistat, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you have diabetes, weight loss may improve your blood sugar control. Monitor your blood sugar levels regularly and share the results with your doctor. Orlistat should not be used during pregnancy, as weight loss offers no benefit to pregnant women and may harm the unborn baby. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of orlistat or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If you are taking medications for seizures, orlistat may reduce their effectiveness. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 for severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, or contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Store orlistat at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. For best results, use orlistat alongside a doctor-approved exercise and diet plan. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, but skip it if it has been more than one to two hours since your meal, as the medication will no longer be effective. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about orlistat. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
